summary: iter138 backend-only testing of the new clients file import (CSV/XLSX). Created /app/backend/tests/test_iter138_clients_import.py — 19/19 pytest PASS. Covered: CSV `;` and `,` parsing (headers, row_count, preview<=20, rows_full, auto_mapping Nom→name / Téléphone→phone / Email→email / Adresse→address / Code postal→postal_code / Ville→city / Notes→notes, unknown column left unmapped, fields catalogue with name.required=true), XLSX parsing via openpyxl (identical shape), empty file → 400 'Fichier vide', blank-lines-only → 400, unauthenticated parse → 403, execute happy path with field-level persistence check via GET /api/clients, unmapped columns ignored (stored as ''), mapping without 'name' → 400 « La colonne « Nom / Prénom » doit être mappée », empty mapping → 400, invalid duplicate_strategy → 422, row with empty name → skipped 'nom manquant', duplicate by phone strategy=ignore (skipped_count=1, no new doc), strategy=update (updated_count=1, non-empty fields updated, empty field does NOT overwrite, no duplicate doc), strategy=create (2nd doc created), duplicate detected by email alone, 300-row bulk (created_count=300, error_count=0), technicien (no clients.create) → 403 on both endpoints, multi-tenant isolation (Acme cannot see default's imported client and the same phone in Acme is NOT flagged duplicate → dedup is company-scoped). CRITICAL STRICTNESS CHECK PASSED at raw-DB level: snapshotted document counts of every collection before/after an import — only `clients` changed (22→27), zero new collections, no sales/projects/invoices/interventions/planning/notifications/audit docs written. Also verified via API that GET /api/sales and GET /api/projects counts are unchanged before/after both the 3-row and 300-row imports. Volume probe: 2000-row CSV parse = 0.52s / 147 KB response, execute 2000 rows = 3.0s, created_count=2000, no errors. All test data (TEST_IMP_*, TEST_VOL_*, TEST_DBSTRICT_*, stray 'Prenom' client) deleted; db.clients back to its original 22 docs, sales=11 projects=11 unchanged.

minor.issue: Mapping two columns onto the same field silently keeps only the LAST column (field_to_col dict overwrite). E.g. mapping col0='Nom' and col1='Prenom' both to `name` stores only 'Prenom'. With a 'Nom;Prenom' file the user cannot concatenate first+last name; auto-mapping also drops the Prenom column entirely. Consider supporting multi-column concatenation for `name` (or at least warn in the UI).

No cap on `rows` length and one find_one + one insert per row (2000 rows = 3s, sequential). For 'plusieurs milliers' this stays OK but there is no batching/bulk_write and no request-size guard, so a 100k-row payload could block the event loop / exceed body limits. Also no index on clients.phone / clients.email, so dedup lookups are collection scans.

`rows_full` returns the entire file to the browser (147 KB for 2000 rows) and the client posts it all back on execute — duplicate transfer of the whole dataset. A server-side staged upload (or execute-by-file) would scale better.
No audit_logs entry is written for an import (audit_logs count unchanged), while other write paths in the app do log. Bulk client creation/update is worth auditing.
Email is lowercased for dedup but phone is compared raw — '06 00 11 22 33' vs '0600112233' will not match as duplicate. Consider normalizing phone (strip spaces/dots/+33) before the $or lookup.
Unknown extensions fall back to CSV parsing; an .xls (old binary) or .pdf upload returns 200 with garbage headers instead of a clear 400 unsupported-format error.

action_items: Optional: support mapping several columns to `name` (concatenation) — today 'Nom' + 'Prenom' loses the first name.
Optional hardening: cap rows per execute call (e.g. 5000) and/or use bulk_write; add MongoDB indexes on clients.(company_id, phone) and (company_id, email) for dedup performance.
Optional: return 400 for clearly unsupported file types instead of silently CSV-parsing them; normalize phone before duplicate lookup; add an audit_logs entry for imports.
critical_code_review_comments: Strictness requirement is correctly implemented: execute_import_file only touches db.clients (verified by full-DB count diff) — no sale/project/invoice side-effects.

Dedup query uses {'company_id': company_id, '$or': [...]} instead of the shared cq(user) helper; result is correct for admins but bypasses any future scope logic in cq() (e.g. commercial 'own' scope), so a commercial could update/see-as-duplicate another commercial's client. Consider routing through cq(user).
Broad `except Exception` per row swallows real DB errors into `errors[]` and still returns 200 — acceptable for imports but the message is raw str(e) (potential internal detail leak in the response).
server.py is 8241 lines — should be split into routers/modules.
